title: His trombones: the Kong valve-slide and others
summary: The C.G. Conn trombone with one trill valve, later a Holton, and selling one to a circus trombonist.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: What kind of a trombone did you like when you played, what make did you use?

When they made up my mind to play trombone in the band, my people bought innocent model, I believe, the Vell, no, C.G. Kong. Kong. Vell, one Vell. I had a slide drum on me, they paid 85, I had to give it to me. So I had been with them.
Your first instrument was the slide then? No. Wait, I didn't get that straight.
My first instrument was the bass.
It was the bass, I mean your first trombone then. My first trombone was slide.
But it had a trill valve.
Yes. See? I think they called it the end of the trill valve on a Kong trombone, C.G. Kong trombone. It had one vowel.
It was a trill valve. One vowel, yeah. Oh, it went out of the start, I don't think it made so much of a hit.
True valve, did you say something? The one vowel. Just the one for trill.
The slide. For the trill, I see. Yeah, it should.
That's a nice idea. Yeah, I never saw one of those.
I don't think the last one, no. I don't think that was a good make. Did you... I didn't see any others but that one.
Did you have more than one trombone or I mean that was just...
In life, I bought here, I had three trombones. Oh, yeah.
What make did you get next after? Always...

No. The last one was Holt. Holton? A brass. A brass. A brass, yeah. A brass. And then I didn't have that long before I quit. And had a fellow playing the... Used to go through every yard on a circus like that. He was one of those circus trombone players. And I was getting ready to start playing trombone. And on his way through on the circus, I asked him about playing. And he said he had to go to Tulsa Oklahoma to put his shoe up. And when he get there he was riding it. So he did. And I brought him on to New Orleans, you see. And he played trombone while I was trying to play a drum. Yes. And I sold it to him for $25. He paid me $5. But the reason I gave it to him, because when he got there, I didn't have the weight that I thought I would have had, you know, to give him. And he didn't have a good horn. So I didn't give him a horn show and let him go over somebody else. He did that.
